Album / Artist: Gravity Freeze / Little Barrie

Label: Easy Eye Sound

Release Date: May 22, 2026

Review Date: 10/4/2026

Reviewer: DJ Stace

General Comments / Reviews:

Greasy, low-slung Easy Eye Sound garage soul from a 70’s that never was. They turned the heat down a notch, but Cadogan's guitar still bites. Low-slung grooves and bursts of guitar. - DJ Stace

Release Notes:

Sixth album from the London trio led by guitarist Barrie Cadogan; new drummer Coote joins.

Recorded at Rat Salad Studios in Hornsey, North London, with Rupert Lyddon engineering and co-producing.

released May 22, 2026

FCCs: None found

RIYL: The Black Keys, Allah-Las, Oh Sees, The Mystery Lights, El Michels Affair, Skinshape

Play: All, Favs Rated with up to *****

Tracklist:

1. ***** More Bad Miles Of Road 03:49 - Upper-mid pace, slinky and naughty wah-wah pedal heavy funk burlesque rock. Lead single; announced the album in February 2026. Heavy play on Library Show as a single. Sourced: First single. Cadogan started from the bass line, wanting an upright bass sound (The Listening Post); Stark, menacing blues-rock with standup bass (AllMusic).
2. *** It Isn't Soul 02:49 - Slow slinky with fuzzy guitar backing and bright guitar along the top. Great mix of dirt and polish. At home in a Tarantino film in a few years. Sourced: Fuzz-heavy, with dappled psychedelia (Tinnitist).
3. December 05:08 - Upbeat high-hat pace, echoing vocals. This one threw its go-go boots in the corner and is dancing barefoot. Sourced: Nearly pretty ballad with a tenderness the rest of the record lacks (AllMusic); Wistful, Shuggie Otis-styled (Tinnitist); Backing vocals by Holly Quin-Ankrah and Frida Touray (Bandcamp credits).
4. ***** Luggin' Hurt 07:08 - “Do do do, de bap bap badada do,...” Shuffling R&B rhythm and licorice taffy guitar stretching all over 7 minutes of ass-shaking funky wah-riff perfect. Play this song and people will ask “who is this?” If you’re going to spend 7 minutes of your show on a single, it better be good. This one is worth the minutes. Sourced: Named an album highlight (Song Bar).
5. Talk It Up Like It's Wanted 03:02 - Mid-tempo, unremarkable guitar solo shuffler. Sourced: Laid-back and swaying, guitar moving between mellow strumming and murky soloing (AllMusic); 1960s-style fuzz bass as a subtle hook (Derek See).
6. ** Anything You Are 03:20 - Slow and slinky. Rhythm flits around under the strumming R&B guitar and smoky jazz club vocals. Picks up the pace at 1:30 a little. Sourced: Slow shuffle showing Cadogan's take on his blues influences (Bucks Music Group).
7. *** Coralisa 04:49 - Great backbeat based rhythm, with buzzing guitar work over the top. Lightly reminiscent of Jon Spencer Blues Explosion. Sourced: Open space for gnarly guitar workouts and nimble, almost flamenco-style picking (AllMusic).
8. Wire 03:37 - Another uptempo backbeat based slightly buzzy krauty? Sourced: Chugging steam-train rhythm (Song Bar); Cadogan wanted a hypnotic, almost dance-like feel with swampy guitar over Tony Coote's steady groove (Tinnitist); Co-producer Rupert Lyddon plays synth (Bandcamp credits).
9. ** Gravity Freeze 03:07 - Another R&B Funk hip swayer. Sourced: Title refers to sleep paralysis, per Cadogan (Guitar World); Subdued soundtrack for a bad dream (AllMusic).
